name: Phosphene
description: An experimental neural-feed work by the artist collective Orchard Null in which the viewer inhabits no single protagonist but instead experiences eighty-seven minutes as a distributed sensory field — light perceived as sound, sound as texture, the emotional states of a crowd rendered as weather patterns moving through the body. There is no plot in any conventional sense; the piece documents a single afternoon in a Tier 1 market district, but the experiential translation makes it feel geological in scale. It requires a BCI calibration profile unavailable on standard consumer hardware.
cultural_impact: Phosphene became the defining work of the Sensory Dissolution movement and remains the most discussed and least-seen film in M88 art history, with authenticated viewings numbering fewer than nine hundred.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 neurologist has been quietly treating Phosphene viewers for three years and has compiled evidence of a deliberate encoding in the feed — but by whom and for what purpose is unclear.
Orchard Null has announced a second work and is looking for volunteer subjects for the neural-capture process; the call is circulating on underground mesh.
A corporate IP division claims Orchard Null stole proprietary sensory-translation code — and the lawsuit would expose what that code was originally designed for.
